doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Homogenized playing and the individual sounds of the old masters
summary: Players once had instantly identifiable sounds, like Ben Webster, Zoot Sims and Vic Dickenson; a comparison with golf schools.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You know I mean I think a lot of the trouble today is that the playing becomes too homogenized. Too many people sound alike. But you know I’m very interested in golf, and that’s what’s happening with golf too, because people go to golf school and they all come out with the same swing and they all look the same and they all play the same, they all play the same way. And for instance in the old days you could tell a musician by his vibrato. Ben Webster had a different vibrato completely to Lester Young or Coleman Hawkins or Don Byas or Lucky Thompson. Each one had an individual sound. You could tell. Two notes from Zoot Sims and you know that was Zoot. Two notes from Stan Getz and you knew that was Stan and it couldn’t be anybody else. That was who they were. That doesn’t happen anymore. You could identify Roy Eldridge. Last night I was sitting in one of the intermissions and they played a record of Prez. And I was just reminiscing about Vic Dickinson. I used to go every Wednesday to hear Vic Dickinson because his © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -11-

style was so personal. Playing out the side of his mouth and play all those beautiful things that he used to play, but it was so personal and so real. And that band, with Roy Eldridge and Prez and Vic Dickinson, sounded amazing. And they were three completely identifiable people. Conte Candoli said, “that can only be Little Jazz.”
As you say, they were all giants but they were all playing together.
Yes. And I think that made the music better too. They weren’t playing from some five star hotel with a corporate account and all that kind of stuff. It was different.
